sources.title: Grammatica napoletana
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Detailed paradigms (articles, neuter, possessives, verbs incl. essere/avé/tené, avé 'a, metaphony, crasis ô/â/ê). Some sections flagged as needing sources; a few forms marked by the article itself as not used in Naples (e.g. Nolan velarization, sevo/seva); those were NOT adopted.
sources.relevant_sections: Articoli; Sostantivi (metafonia, neutro, raddoppiamento); Aggettivi (dimostrativi, possessivi); Preposizioni; Pronomi; Verbi

sources.title: Lingua napoletana
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.relevant_sections: Fonetica e ortografia (vowel system, schwa, consonants, orthography table)

sources.title: Neapolitan language
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Good summary of articles, neuter 'o + doubling ('o nnapulitano vs 'o napulitano), list of doubling triggers, accent/circumflex conventions, avé as sole active auxiliary. Bibliography cites Iandolo 2001 and De Blasi & Imperatore 2001.
sources.relevant_sections: Alphabet and pronunciation; Grammar (articles, verbal conjugation, doubled initial consonants)

sources.title: Vocabolario napolitano-toscano domestico di arti e mestieri
sources.author: Raffaele D'Ambra
sources.publisher: Napoli (a spese dell'autore); digitized by Google, hosted on Internet Archive
sources.reliability_notes: Read via the Internet Archive OCR full text (djvu.txt); OCR is noisy, entries were checked in context. Key entry: 'Guallara, Guallera sf. Ernia' with 'Abbottare la guallara' (to feel envy) and 'Abboffare la guallera' (to annoy). Uses 19th-century spelling (lo/la articles, -are infinitives).
sources.relevant_sections: Guallara/Guallera, Guallaruso, Assaje, Scetare, Pazziare, Appicciare, Accattare, Jastemma, Mannaggia

sources.title: Vocabolario napoletano-italiano
sources.author: Raffaele Andreoli
sources.publisher: Paravia, Torino; hosted on Internet Archive (PHAIDRA scan)
sources.reliability_notes: Read via Internet Archive OCR full text; OCR noisy. Used to verify headwords and senses (guaglione, nisciuno, overo, neh, uh, mannaggia l'anema toja, curnuto, cuglione, fetente, mappina, alluccare, nguajare, scetare, faticare, assaje, ampressa, guallaruso, jastemma, murtià, mmalora, sciò, vattenne).

sources.title: Vocabolario napolitano-italiano tascabile ... preceduto da brevi osservazioni grammaticali
sources.author: Pietro Paolo Volpe
sources.publisher: Napoli; digitized by Google, hosted on Internet Archive
sources.reliability_notes: Only the introductory 'Brevi osservazioni grammaticali' were used (sound correspondences b>v, d>r, nd>nn, pl>chi, bi>j, fi>sci, glide insertion pajese/voje; article and plural doubling). OCR very noisy.

sources.title: Proverbi napoletani
sources.author: Wikiquote contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Large collection, many items cite printed sources (e.g. 'I Proverbi di Napoli'). Spelling is not uniform and a few items are from other Campanian varieties (u/i articles): only items in city-Neapolitan form were adopted. Meanings rewritten in our own words.

sources.title: Modi di dire napoletani
sources.author: Wikiquote contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Idioms with explanations and references to printed works (Apicella 'Il frasario napoletano', 'Manuale di napoletanità', contemporary novels). Key: 'Me staje abbuffanno 'a guallera' (annoy to death) and hyperbolic variants ''a guallara a pezzaiuola', 'sfaccimma', 'cazzimma', 'chiaveca'. Meanings rewritten.

sources.title: Wiktionary Neapolitan and Italian entries (machine-readable extract by kaikki.org)
sources.author: Wiktionary contributors; extraction by Tatu Ylonen (wiktextract)
sources.reliability_notes: Neapolitan coverage is thin and mixes regional forms; used only for corroboration: cazzimma (borrowed into Italian from Neapolitan, from cazzo + -imma; cynical opportunism / gratuitous malice), ricchione (vulgar derogatory slur), guaglione, ajere, dimane, accussì, chiagnere.

sources.title: Appuniscë a parlesia? Uno studio sui posteggiatori napoletani e il loro gergo (tesi di laurea magistrale)
sources.author: Anna Fortunato
sources.license: All rights reserved (thesis repository, open access)
sources.reliability_notes: Chapter 2.2 summarizes Radtke (I dialetti della Campania, 1997), Loporcaro (2009) and Cortelazzo et al. (I dialetti italiani, 2002): Southern metaphony, masculine/neuter distinction, doubling after neuter and feminine-plural articles and plural/neuter clitics, partitive n'amico d''o mio, -iello/-ella and -imma suffixes, enclitic possessives (mammeta), tené = possess / stà = locative be, prepositional accusative, jamme ja, ca as polyvalent complementizer, hypothetical clauses with subjunctive in both clauses.

sources.title: Italian Wikipedia articles: Facite ammuina; Scugnizzo; Guappo; Inciucio; Fica (section on regional names: pucchiacca)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Short lead definitions only: ammuina = confusione; scugnizzo = monello di strada napoletano; guappo; 'nciucio/'nciucià = pettegolezzo/spettegolare; pucchiacca = Neapolitan vulgar term for vulva (article Fica). Other URLs: https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scugnizzo, https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guappo, https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inciucio, https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fica

sources.title: Glossary of Neapolitan: the most used and known words in Naples and beyond
sources.reliability_notes: Tourism glossary; used only as corroboration for colloquial items (alluccare, arronzare, arteteca, appiccecarse, ammuccarse, cazzimma, chiattillo, 'nzallanuto, 'nziria, 'nzisto, sarchiapone, scuorno, vrenzola, vattere, lloco).

sources.title: La frutta realistica ci ha fatto la uallera, video virale
sources.reliability_notes: Contemporary press attestation of the spelling 'uallera' and of the phrase 'ci ha fatto la uallera' glossed as 'ci ha stufato oltre ogni immaginazione'.
